newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil ends slightly off but supported by heating oil.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil ends slightly off but supported by heating oil.

text.p: IPE gas oil closed slightly lower on Thursday but a strong performance by NYMEX heating oil pulled the contract off lows, brokers said.
May gas oil ended the session 50 cents down at $162.25 a tonne, off a low of $161.75.
"It wasn't particularly startling over here but heat looked strong...although it has ticked off the highs," said one broker.
Both NYMEX heating oil and gasoline held key technical support levels and reversed early losses made on sentiment of ample supplies.
Heating oil demand in the U.S. Northeast is expected rise over the next few days due to cold weather conditions, the worst of which should last until Saturday, forecasters said.

Sun Co Inc, a major supplier of heating oil in the region, said on Thursday that the cold spell had already cleared out its stocks and it was unlikely to resume supplies to distributors until late next week.
NYMEX May heating oil was trading 0.42 cents up at 53.90 a gallon at 1650 GMT, off the session high of 54.60.
June Brent was steady at $17.81 a barrel, having drifted off a high of $17.95 made in the wake of product gains.
